input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps! What do I need to do next?
Yes, it’s the phone with the number 555-123-2002 that’s having the problem. That’s the one I use. What should I do now?
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see an airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What does that mean?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but it says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. I still don’t see any bars or 4G/5G symbols. What should I do next?
It says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. Does that mean something’s wrong with my SIM card? What should I do now?

I reseated the SIM card like you said. Now, I see one bar for signal and it says “2G,” but it still says “Data Disabled.” I haven’t tried sending an MMS yet—should I try now, or is there something else I need to do first?
I turned on mobile data, and now it says “Data Enabled,” but it still shows just one bar and “2G” at the top. I don’t see anything about 3G, 4G, or 5G. What should I do next?

I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now I see full bars and “5G” at the top, with “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to do first?
I just tried, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. It’s a bit frustrating—everything looks like it should work now. What should I do next?
I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet,” but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. I’m not sure what that means—do I need to change something here?
I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send pictures again?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending a picture message again?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried again, but I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all this.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any service or line-related problems. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the steps to resolve your MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps! What do I need to do next?

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need to confirm which phone line you’re using, since your account has multiple lines. Is your MMS problem happening on the phone with the number 555-123-2002, or is it a different number on your account?

Once you confirm, I’ll guide you through some quick checks and steps to get your picture messaging working again.
Yes, it’s the phone with the number 555-123-2002 that’s having the problem. That’s the one I use. What should I do now?

Thank you for confirming. To start troubleshooting your MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a quick check on your phone. Please use your phone to check if you can send MMS messages by running the “can_send_mms” diagnostic tool or feature (if available in your device’s support or diagnostic menu).

Let me know the result, or if you need instructions on how to access this feature. This will help us determine the next steps to resolve your MMS problem.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your messaging app cannot send MMS messages, let’s go through a few steps to identify and resolve the issue. First, we need to make sure your phone has both cellular service and mobile data enabled, as both are required for MMS.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (indicating cellular service)
- If mobile data is enabled (look for 4G, 5G, LTE, or similar icons)
- If Airplane Mode is on (an airplane icon)

Let me know what you see, and we’ll proceed from there.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see an airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means Airplane Mode is currently enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off, which prevents you from sending MMS messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons (like 4G, 5G, or LTE) reappear. Then, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works or if you still have issues.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but it says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. I still don’t see any bars or 4G/5G symbols. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you’re seeing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” it looks like your phone isn’t connecting to the cellular network yet, which is required for MMS.

Let’s check if your SIM card is being recognized by your phone. Please use your phone’s diagnostic feature to check the SIM card status (look for an option like “check SIM status” in your device’s support or diagnostic menu).

Let me know what the SIM status says (e.g., Active, Missing, or Locked), and I’ll guide you on the next steps.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. Does that mean something’s wrong with my SIM card? What should I do now?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it usually means the SIM card is not properly seated or recognized by your device. This can often be fixed by reseating the SIM card.

Please follow these steps:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card tray and take out the SIM card.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly aligned.
4. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if the SIM card is now detected and if you have signal bars or mobile data icons. Let me know what you see, and if you’re able to send MMS messages now.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I reseated the SIM card like you said. Now, I see one bar for signal and it says “2G,” but it still says “Data Disabled.” I haven’t tried sending an MMS yet—should I try now, or is there something else I need to do first?

Thank you for reseating the SIM card. Since you now have a signal (even if it’s just one bar) and see “2G,” but “Data Disabled,” there are still a couple of things we need to address before testing MMS:

1. MMS requires at least a 3G network and mobile data to be enabled. Since you’re on 2G and data is disabled, let’s first enable mobile data on your phone.
2. After enabling mobile data, we should also change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G, which will improve your connection and support MMS.

Please enable mobile data on your phone (usually found in your phone’s quick settings or network settings). Once you’ve done that, let me know if you see a 3G, 4G, or 5G icon and if “Data Enabled” appears in your status bar. If not, I’ll guide you through changing your network mode preference.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I turned on mobile data, and now it says “Data Enabled,” but it still shows just one bar and “2G” at the top. I don’t see anything about 3G, 4G, or 5G. What should I do next?

Since your phone is still connected to a 2G network, which is not suitable for MMS, let’s update your network mode preference to allow your phone to connect to 4G or 5G networks if available.

Please go to your phone’s network settings and look for an option like “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.” Set it to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G preferred” if available.

After changing this setting, check your status bar again to see if it now shows 3G, 4G, or 5G, and if your signal improves. Let me know what you see, and then we’ll try sending an MMS.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now I see full bars and “5G” at the top, with “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to do first?

That’s great progress! Now that you have full bars, “5G,” and “Data Enabled,” your phone is properly connected and ready for MMS.

Please try sending a picture message (MMS) now. Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you encounter any issues. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll check your APN settings next.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. It’s a bit frustrating—everything looks like it should work now. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your connection is now good but MMS still isn’t working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Please use your phone’s diagnostic feature to check the APN settings (look for “check APN settings” in your device’s support or diagnostic menu). Pay special attention to whether the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL is set.

Let me know if the APN settings or MMSC URL appear to be missing or incorrect, and I’ll guide you on how to reset them.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet,” but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. I’m not sure what that means—do I need to change something here?

The missing MMSC URL is likely the reason you can’t send MMS messages. To fix this, you’ll need to reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier.

Please follow these steps:
1. Go to your phone’s network or mobile data settings.
2. Find the option to reset APN settings (it may be labeled “Reset to default” or “Reset APN”).
3. Confirm the reset.

After resetting the APN settings, you must restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Please do this now, and then try sending an MMS message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have issues.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send pictures again?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. There are still a few more things we can check to resolve your MMS issue:

1. Let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, as it can sometimes interfere with MMS. Please check your phone’s settings for Wi-Fi Calling and let me know if it is turned ON.
2. If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF and try sending an MMS again.

Let me know the status of Wi-Fi Calling and if turning it off helps. If MMS still doesn’t work after this, we’ll continue troubleshooting further.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending a picture message again?

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling on your phone. After you’ve turned it off, try sending a picture message (MMS) again.

Let me know if you’re able to send the MMS successfully after turning off Wi-Fi Calling, or if you still encounter any issues.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried again, but I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all this.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. I understand this process can be overwhelming, and I want to make sure your issue gets resolved.

At this point, since we’ve checked your network connection, SIM card, APN settings, and Wi-Fi Calling, and you’re still unable to send MMS messages, this may require more advanced technical support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can assist you further and ensure your MMS issue is resolved. Please hold on while I connect you.
